answer: Policies are written in sonnet, settled in river, and ripple lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 45% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 79 aliases cost 231 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
